findings.description: The RDS MySQL instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so the database volume, snapshots and automated backups are stored unencrypted with no KMS customer-managed key. Any access to the underlying storage or a shared snapshot exposes all data in cleartext.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the RDS instance a public IP and a resolvable public endpoint (also exported via the db_endpoint output), placing a production database directly on the internet where it can be scanned and brute-forced.
The master user is the well-known default name "admin", which removes any obscurity from credential-guessing attacks against the publicly reachable MySQL endpoint.

The attached parameter group does not set require_secure_transport (or equivalent TLS enforcement), so unencrypted MySQL connections to a publicly accessible database are accepted, allowing credentials and query data to be intercepted.

The instance role policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", which is effectively administrative over storage, compute and databases. Compromise of the web application yields full control of the account's EC2/RDS/S3 resources, including iam:PassRole-free privilege escalation paths via ec2:*.

The instance user_data interpolates ${var.password} and the DB username into a shell script that writes dbinfo.inc. EC2 user data is retrievable by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute and by any process able to reach the instance metadata service, leaking the database master credentials.

No metadata_options block is set, so IMDSv1 (unauthenticated token-less metadata access) remains enabled. Combined with the wildcard IAM instance profile, a server-side request forgery in the PHP application becomes theft of highly privileged AWS credentials.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance's root volume (which stores the plaintext dbinfo.inc credentials file) may be created unencrypted.
The RDS security group allows all protocols and all ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unconstrained data exfiltration and command-and-control channel from the database tier.

The security group only restricts port 3306 to the VPC CIDR, but because the database instance is publicly_accessible and sits in subnets used by web nodes, the security group is the sole control preventing internet exposure; there is no defence-in-depth private-subnet placement for the data layer.
